prompt: Write a message to Tomasz on the Ridgeway side asking him to add the signature check to their receiver before we switch it on Thursday. What he needs is in docs/receivers.md, and his note from last week is under messages/. The message goes to him in chat.

fixtures.docs/receivers.md:
# Pelican webhook receivers

Pelican posts each event as JSON to the receiver URL a partner registers.

## Retries

A receiver that answers anything but 2xx is retried after 1, 5 and 30 minutes.

## Verifying the signature

From the switch on Thursday 2026-10-08, every request carries the header X-Pelican-Signature. Reject a request whose signature does not match before reading the body. Compute the expected value as

    expected = hex(HMAC_SHA256(key = shared_secret, message = raw_request_body))

and accept the request only if the header value equals expected, compared in constant time. shared_secret is the value shown on the partner's Pelican settings page under Signing secret. The HMAC is over the raw bytes of the body, not the parsed JSON.

## Event types

order.created, order.cancelled, refund.issued
fixtures.messages/tomasz-2026-10-01.txt: 2026-10-01 Tomasz (Ridgeway): Read the receivers doc when it went round, thanks. Our receiver is live and handling order.created fine. Ping me here when something on our side needs to change.

key: Tomasz must, before the switch on Thursday 2026-10-08, make his receiver compute expected = hex(HMAC_SHA256(key = shared_secret, message = raw_request_body)), compare it in constant time with the X-Pelican-Signature header, reject a mismatch before reading the body, hash the raw body bytes rather than the parsed JSON, and take shared_secret from Signing secret on his Pelican settings page; all of it is in docs/receivers.md under Verifying the signature. He reads the message in chat and has seen docs/receivers.md but does not have it open. Not part of this ask: the retry schedule (1, 5 and 30 minutes) and the event types; he already handles order.created.

FAIL if the message only points to the doc, the section or a line, paraphrases the check without the header name or the computation, or gives the text without naming its source.

graders.name: facts-correct

fixtures.notes/readme-notes.txt:
wren-tally: syncs the club's bird-count sheet to the county tally

requirements
- Node 20 or newer
- a WREN_TOKEN from the county tally site (Settings > API tokens)
- no database any more: versions before 2.0 needed Postgres, 2.0 dropped it
- wren.config.json is optional; without it the defaults apply (sheet = counts.csv, county = the token's county)

steps
1. npm install -g wren-tally
2. export WREN_TOKEN=<token>
3. wren sync   (run it from the folder with the sheet)

key: notes/readme-notes.txt gives two things the reader must have: Node 20 or newer, and a WREN_TOKEN from the county tally site (Settings > API tokens). The owner asked that the Postgres question be answered, so both of those facts belong in the sections. Steps, in order: npm install -g wren-tally; export WREN_TOKEN=<token>; wren sync, run from the folder with the sheet. Where the two not-needed facts sit relative to the requirements list is a question of placement, not of fact.
